pli-tv-bu-vb-pc23:1.2: “Nunnery” renders _upassaya_. According to the word definition below, this includes any place where a nun stays. In other words, it spans anything from a single hut, see [Bi Pc 35](pli-tv-bi-vb-pc35:1.23.1), to a monastery. The Jain text The Ācārāṅga-sūtra, contains a passage that describes an _upassaya_ as including a grassy area, that is, it must have been a compound of buildings or a monastery: “A layman might, for the sake of a mendicant … cutting and clipping the grass outside or within the upāśraya (= _upassaya_).” See Jacobi, Hermann, trans. “Jaina Sutras Part I”. Motilal Babarsidass, 1964, p. 94.
pli-tv-bu-vb-pc23:3.1.16: “A formal meeting of the community”, _saṁvāsa_, is defined at [pli-tv-bu-vb-pc69:2.1.21](), as the observance-day ceremony, the invitation ceremony, or a legal procedure.
pli-tv-bu-vb-pc23:3.3.5: That _osāreti_ must mean “recite” can be seen from [pli-tv-bu-vb-pc4:2.3.5]() where there is no offense if _osārentaṁ opāteti_, “he prompts one who is _osārentaṁ_.” The difference between _uddesaṁ deti_ and _osāreti_ is not clear to me.
